Scenario: Inflation Persistence Forces Further Rate Hikes
Description: Persistent inflation pressures lead the Federal Reserve to implement an additional 50 bps rate hike, resulting in a bear steepening of the yield curve and wider credit spreads.
Rationale: Recent inflation data remains above target, forcing the Fed to tighten policy further. Higher rates increase funding costs and duration risk, pressuring LCR and NII.
Assumptions: Inflation remains sticky; Fed prioritizes price stability over growth; deposit outflows as clients seek higher yields.

Description: Inflation stabilizes near 3%, allowing the Fed to pause and maintain current rates. The curve flattens modestly and credit spreads tighten slightly.
Rationale: Inflation expectations are anchored, and economic growth is steady. The Fed adopts a wait-and-see approach, supporting stable funding and moderate NII.
Assumptions: Inflation moderates without new shocks; deposit base remains stable; no major regulatory changes.

Description: Escalating geopolitical risks trigger a flight to quality, causing a sharp widening of MBS basis and modest deposit outflows.
Rationale: Market volatility rises as geopolitical events unfold. Investors move to USTs, but MBS valuations suffer and some clients withdraw deposits for liquidity.
Assumptions: Geopolitical shocks drive risk-off sentiment; depositors seek liquidity; MBS underperform.

Description: New regulatory guidance clarifies HQLA eligibility, allowing banks to optimize portfolios and improve liquidity metrics.
Rationale: Clearer rules reduce uncertainty, enabling more efficient HQLA allocation and supporting LCR/NSFR improvement.
Assumptions: Regulatory changes are well-communicated and phased in; no major market disruptions.

Scenario: Positive Economic Data Drive Market Optimism
Description: Unexpectedly strong economic data boosts risk appetite, resulting in a bull steepening of the yield curve and tighter credit spreads.
Rationale: Robust growth surprises markets, supporting credit and equity markets. Deposit inflows increase as confidence rises.
Assumptions: No inflation resurgence; Fed remains on hold; deposit base grows with economic optimism.
